 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice V.Gopala Krishna Rao

entities.text: United India Insurance Co. Ltd., vs Padiri Guramma
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The appellant is 2nd respondent/Insurance company and the respondents are claim petitioners and
respondent No.1 in M.V.O.P.No.57 of 2010 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims
Tribunal-cum-III Additional District Judge, Tirupati.

entities.text:
Motor Accident Claims
Tribunal-cum-III Additional District Judge, Tirupati
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The appellant filed the appeal questioning the legal validity of the order of the Tribunal.
2. For the sake of convenience, both the parties in the appeal will be referred to as they are arrayed in the claim application.

3. The claim petitioners filed the petition under Section 166 (1)
(c) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 claiming compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- for the death of P.
Surendranath Reddy in a motor vehicle accident that took place on 19.09.2009.
VGKR,J MACMA No.848 of 2013 4.

The brief averments in the petition filed by the petitioners are as follows:
On 19.09.2009 at about 12.30 p.m. the deceased was going on his Bajaj Motor Cycle bearing registration No.AP 03 6170 from Piler side to Tirupati side and when he reached Sree Vidyanikethan Engineering College, Chandragiri Mandal, a car bearing registration No.AP 03R 3587 being driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner, came in opposite direction and dashed the motor cycle of the deceased resulting in the instantaneous death of the deceased.

entities.text: Sree Vidyanikethan Engineering College, Chandragiri Mandal
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The 1st respondent is owner and the 2nd respondent is insurer of the offending car.
Hence, both the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
5. The 1st respondent filed a counter.

He contended that he sold away the offending car to one D.
Kannamma on 07.03.2009 and therefore, he has no liability since then.
6. The 2nd respondent also filed a counter by denying the manner of accident.

It is pleaded that the deceased was riding the motor VGKR,J cycle in a rash and negligent manner at high speed and lost control over it and dashed the left side iron barricades and succumbed to head injury and the car was never involved in the accident much less on 19.09.2009.
Therefore, the Insurance company is not liable to pay compensation.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Based on the above pleadings of both the parties, the following issues were settled for trial by the Tribunal:
1) Whether the accident occurred due to negligence of the driver of Ambassador Car bearing Regn.No.AP 03R 3587 that resulted in causing the death of Padiri Surendranath Reddy?
2) Whether the petitioners are the legal representatives of deceased and entitled to compensation and if so, to what amount and payable from whom?

3) To what relief?
8.
During the course of enquiry in the claim petition, on behalf of the petitioners, P.Ws.1 to 3 were examined and Exs.A.1 to A.5 were marked.

On behalf of the respondents, R.W.1 was examined and Exs.B.1 and B.2 were marked.
VGKR,J 9.

At the culmination of the enquiry, based on the material available on record, the Tribunal came to a conclusion that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the car and accordingly, granted an amount of Rs.5,19,000/- with interest at 7.5% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of deposit against the respondents.
Aggrieved against the said order, the appellant/Insurance company preferred the present appeal.
10. Heard learned counsels for both the parties.

11. The appellant pleaded that the Tribunal failed to consider that the 1st respondent sold the offending car to one D.Kannamma and not to G.Gunasekhar and erred in relying on Ex.A.2 for determining the ownership of the insured vehicle.

12. Now, the point for determination is:
Whether the order of the Tribunal needs any interference of this Court?
VGKR,J 13.
POINT:
In order to prove the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending car, the petitioners relied on the evidence of P.Ws.1 and 2.
P.W.1 is not an eye witness to the accident.
P.W.2 is an eye witness to the accident.

He deposed that he witnessed the accident and the driver of the offending car drove the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner and hit the motor cycle of the deceased, as a result of which, the deceased fell down on the road and sustained head injury and died on the spot.
There is nothing in the cross-examination of P.W.2 to discredit his evidence and the suggestions put to him were denied by him.
The petitioners also relied on Ex.A.1-certified copy of first information report and Ex.A.2- certified copy of charge sheet.

Ex . A.1 goes to show that first United India Insurance Co. Ltd., vs Padiri Guramma on 10 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/150326882/
2 information report was registered against the driver of the offending car.

entities.text: United India Insurance Co. Ltd., vs Padiri Guramma
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Ex.A.2 clearly goes to show that after completion of investigation, the Investigating Officer filed a charge sheet against the driver of the offending car.
The evidence of P.W.1 coupled with Exs.A.1 and A.2 clearly proves about the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending car resulting in the accident.
The VGKR,J learned Tribunal also, on appreciating the evidence on record, came to conclusion that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending car.
This Court feels that there is no need to interfere with the said finding given by the learned Tribunal.
14. As per Ex.A.3-certified copy of post mortem report and Ex.A.4- certified copy of inquest report and as per the case of the petitioners, the age of the deceased was 42 years.
The multiplier applicable to the age group of the deceased is "14" as per the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Sarla Varma case.
The dependants on the deceased are five in number.

The Tribunal by giving cogent reasons fixed the monthly income of the deceased as Rs.4,000/- and after deducting 1/3rd income towards personal expenses of the deceased, arrived the loss of dependency to the family of the deceased at Rs.5,04,000/- (Rs.3,000/- x 12 months x 14).
Besides, the Tribunal awarded Rs.5,000/- towards funeral expenses and Rs.10,000/- towards loss of consortium to the 1st VGKR,J petitioner/wife of the deceased.
In total, the Tribunal granted compensation of Rs.5,19,000/-.
Therefore, there is no need to interfere with the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal.

15. The learned Tribunal in its order held that the 2nd respondent is the insurer of the offending car under Ex.B.1 policy and the policy was also in force as on the date of the accident and the Insurance company failed to establish that the conditions of the policy are violated and therefore, both the respondents are liable to pay compensation to the claim petitioners.
This Court feels that there is no illegality in the said finding recorded by the learned Tribunal.
16. In view of the foregoing reasons, this Court finds that there are no merits in the appeal and the appeal is devoid of merits and it is liable to be dismissed.

17. Accordingly, the appeal is dismissed, while confirming the decree and order dated 09.10.2012 passed by the Chairman, Motor VGKR,J Accident Claims Tribunal-cum-III Additional District Judge, Tirupati, in M.V.O.P.No.57 of 2010.
